subject: BlueLeaf - post-demo recap & proposed quality probe plan
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@blueleaf.ai>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueLeaf - post-demo recap & proposed quality probe plan

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid details on your MLP inference pain points and the latency/cost targets you called out. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from demo:
- Primary goal: migrate two production inference routes (summary and entity-extraction) to a cheaper, stable runtime without increasing hallucination risk.
- Current constraints: p50 latency budget 120ms, burst up to 800 rps during morning window, PII policy prevents persisted request logs outside VPC.
- Competitive context: you ran a small test on HyperscaleX and saw lower per-token cost but ~3x the hallucination rate on multi-sentence prompts.

Proposed immediate experiment (what we can run in parallel with your team):
1) Short probe suite (3–5 days) comparing Redwood-hosted model variant vs HyperscaleX baseline across your 250 proprietary prompts. Metrics: exact-match entity F1, hallucination rate (assertion of unsupported facts), and p95 latency.
2) A small regression check using your flagged failure set (the 12 examples from last week) to validate mitigation behavior for hallucinations.
3) Cost/ops snapshot: token-level cost estimates and a digest of fallback behavior under capacity loss.

Artifacts attached: probe matrix (blueleaf-probe-matrix.xlsx), sample prompts (sample_prompts_v2.txt), initial SGL cost estimate (sgl-cost-estimate.pdf).

Asks for BlueLeaf:
- Send the 250-prompt CSV and the 12-case failure set (or confirm we can pull from the shared drive link below).
- Confirm a 4-hour window next week when your devs can run side-by-side calls (we'll provide a small script and instructions).

Internal notes: looping in Marissa to scope the probe automation and Hannah to confirm commercial framing if the probe looks good. Rishi — can you prepare quick quantization/latency notes for the summary route?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@blueleaf.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@blueleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 17:01:34 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueLeaf - post-demo recap & proposed quality probe plan

Camila — great recap, thanks. A couple clarifying points before we schedule the test window: 

1) The 250 prompts: these include both short (one-liner) and long multi-paragraph prompts. Our hypothesis is that HyperscaleX degrades only on longer context. Would Redwood’s probe separate by prompt length buckets?
2) Hallucination definition: we currently flag anything where the model asserts a fact contradicted by our canonical knowledge base. Can you adopt the same comparator?
3) Data controls: because of our PII policy, any request/response logs must stay within our VPC. Is the Redwood Private option required for the probe or can we run an isolated logging configuration on hosted?

We can push the prompts to the Drive folder you linked. For the 4-hour window, mornings are better (8–12 PT).

—Daniel
Director of Product, BlueLeaf Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 18:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueLeaf - post-demo recap & proposed quality probe plan

Looping in technical plan. Quick answers and plan of attack: 

- Prompt buckets: yes — we'll instrument buckets (short: <64 tokens, medium: 64–256, long: >256) and report per-bucket metrics. That should surface the HyperscaleX degradation Daniel mentioned.
- Hallucination comparator: we can take your KB as the oracle. For the probe we'll run an automatic KB-checker (exact-match + fuzzy lookup) and then surface cases for manual review. Please provide KB export or an API endpoint read-only token.
- Data controls: for the probe we can run with hosted but with zero retention (request/response ephemeral logs) and ship a PCR (probe) artifact that resides only in your Drive. If BlueLeaf policy requires guaranteed VPC-only logs, we should schedule a short Private trial (2-week) — commercial terms can be scoped later.

Actions I will take:
- Prepare the probe harness (script + Docker image) and an instructions README.
- Add a column in the probe matrix for 'hyperscaler-variant' so we can match tokens/latency side-by-side.

Rishi — can you draft a two-paragraph note on quant/quantization tradeoffs for the summary model (how INT8 vs Q4 affects hallucination vs latency) and attach as a short doc?

Camila — when you confirm the window, I'll schedule infra and reserve the test runners.

-Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@blueleaf.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 09:04:21 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueLeaf - post-demo recap & proposed quality probe plan

Perfect — we'll upload the 250 prompts and the 12-case failure set to the Drive folder by EOD today.

For the KB export: Sara can share a read-only endpoint token in the folder (it only exposes the canonical facts table). For now, let's start with the hosted zero-retention probe on Monday 8:00 AM PT and we can decide mid-week if we need the Private trial.

Thanks — Daniel
